I'm not as rampantly anti-Alienware as some folks here may be, but I would agree that they are not worth the money. Here are my reasons, based on personal experience:

My previous gaming laptop was an Alienware M17x R3. At the time I bought it, Alienware allowed you to customize nearly every component during the order process, so I was able to purchase the combination of components that fit my particular needs for a gaming laptop. However, when it came time for me to purchase a new one (3 years is my usual cycle), I had already been looking at Alienware again as I had not had much trouble at all with the one I purchased. What I found was not good: since Alienware is owned by Dell, they've gone the same route as other Dell laptops and had become barely customizable. You buy the few tiers they offer and take the stuff you don't need along with the things you do, leading to a laptop that is extremely overpriced.

Alienware also used to be more of a boutique PC seller before they were purchased by Dell and cared a lot more about build quality and did testing of systems before shipping. That also went by the wayside as the company became fully-integrated into Dell corporate culture. Even the one I purchased was already showing signs of mass-production and poor build quality, particularly in the area of cooling, where they use those horrible sticky pads between CPU/GPU and their respective coolers.

Last year I went instead with Digital Storm for my new laptop, and I was able to fully customize nearly every component and they ran my laptop through quality control and testing. My Krypton runs way cooler than my Alienware ever did even when new, and all I need to do when it starts to run hotter is do a thorough dusting and it cools off once more, usually every few months.

My son got my Alienware as a hand-me-down and he's pleased with it as it was an upgrade from his previous Dell laptop, but their products are no longer worth it for me.

While I personally recommend Digital Storm, there are plenty of other good choices for you as well other than Alienware. Coming from someone who has ACTUALLY OWNED AN ALIENWARE LAPTOP I wouldn't recommend one.

I got an Alienware M17xR2 (early 2010 model) in early 2011. I paid about $1600AUD for it second hand and the cheapest I could find them at the time was $3200.

Just putting it out there, the laptop was great and I used it up until 2 weeks ago when I built my first dedicated gaming rig. It got me through University and a whole bunch of LAN parties/gaming nights. Many god times were had using it and it's currently sitting in my room ready to be sold. However it had it's fair share of problems and it was only worth the money because i got it relatively cheaply.

As far as actual build quality and components go I was disappointed and the design was absolutely shithouse. I took mine apart down to the motherboard multiple times and ended up having to fix multiple problems myself.

Look at forums for the issues Alienwares have. In my case the cooling system was severely lacking. The thermal paste and cooling pads were pretty poorly assembled. I ended up renewing the thermal pads and paste. I also had to put tape in between the heatsink and fans just to get the air to pass through the heatsink.

Is this problem in every Alienware model? I don't expect it to be but ask yourself. You're paying several grand for a gaming laptop from a company division (Alienware is owned by Dell) that specialises in such. Is it acceptable to have these glaring problems?

Just do your research, don't look at reviews they will praise the Alienware as the next coming of Jesus. Think IGN and the 7/10 scale. Instead look at the forums and find out what problems people are having.

PS. I often had problems with the charger and the computer wouldn't go into high performance mode unless you turned it off and cleared the cmos This is a problem with all Dell computers as they all match chargers to batteries.

TL;DR Put more R&D effort into cooling and less into light up keyboards and logos. Way too expensive for what you get, cheaper alternatives with similar specs.

My advice, get a refurb enterprise class/ mobile workstation laptop. Not the lightest, but they do have some perks.
1 indestructible. As a student myself, trust me, that thing will get beat up, but most of these machines are designed to be given to stupid employees.
2 great keyboards.
3, most are user repairable to a much greater degree than other laptops.
4. Price; mobile workstations are normally expensive as fuck. Refub they go for pennies. I got a dell precision m4600 a while back, running 8gb memory, nvidia quadro k1000m and an i7 qm (4 physical cores + hyperthreading) for 500.
5, warranty support. This is only a plus when ordering from a specific refurbisher, but HUGE plug to joy systems (the specific refurbisher). My laptop broke a while back (short in the power connector that I initially misdiagnosed as a bad power cord). Let me describe support from joy. First phone call. Without even providing a serial number, I got a shipping label, after a 10 minute call, INCLUDING HOLD TIME. I was also told they would ship a replacement charger when they were told the label was used, not on reviving the package to get me the charger faster. I did not have to send in my laptop. It took me a while to send the cord in, and i didnt get an email or anything indicating a replacement had been sent. so I called up after I did to check that they sent out said cord. Due to a server being down, they didn't know. Response? Overnight me a cord so that it arrives the same day it would have if they had sent it out. When I got that package, there was a 15% off coupon inside, and a handwritten apology from the warehouse staff for "any inconvenience suffered from a possible delay" the next day, the original cord arrived, so they HAD, in fact, shipped it. Upon realizing it was a short in the power jack, not the ac adapter, I called up joy, and again got a shipping label quickly. I also asked if I could take the hard drive out so that I would have access to it. "Sure, go right ahead". 6 days after fedexing it, I got an entirely new machine, which was actually a slight UPGRADE from what I sent in (textured back and keys, which I didn't have before, and faster memory). There was not hard drive in it. In the hard drive bay was a little envelope taped inside with all the screws needed to put it in. At no point was I on the phone for more than 18 minutes and 29 seconds (that call was when they were checking the status of the shipped power cord), and at no point did I even have to read a zero number or anything over the phone. I never paid a dime in shipping or random fees, and all of their reps were polite, helpful, and none of them had strong accents or were difficult to understand. Whenever i called in and gave my reference number, they always asked if I wanted to be transfered to my original representative. I did not use this, but I think that it is a genius way to keep everything clear and straight. By far my best support experience ever, and they have earned some serious plugging, hence this post.

Note that I am not affiliated with joy systems in any way other than owning one of their machines. For those in doubt (since I know this totally looks like a sponsored post), I will provide evidence to that effect.

Edit: a few things I forgot to add.

1, the original system I received looked almost new, except for some orange paint scraped ONTO the side of the system, and the fact that the hard drive had 200 hours of power on time (really not that much), I would never have been able to tell the difference between it and a brand new system. The replacement I received was in PERFECT condition. as in, if it weren't a 4 year old model, and if it weren't for the fact that the hard drive had been removed as per my request I would legitimately think that the shrink wrap it came in was original packaging.

2, The charger that came with the system initially was the wrong type. It was for the previous years precision, compatible, but low wattage, took forever to charge. I mentioned this to my rep the first time around, he made a note of it, and both chargers that I received were of the correct type.
